question: Does the containing Windows VM dedicated GPU-memory usage provide an under14-decimal-GB upper bound during the already-tested productive shared-MTP long profile?
primary_metric: Sum of every dedicated_bytes counter for all enumerated vmwp processes/instances. No alias deduplication and no desktop baseline subtraction. Shared system RAM is separately recorded.
bound_inference: All model/MTP CUDA allocations are in the Docker/WSL VM. The containing VM dedicated-use total is a conservative superset, including private and cross-process shared resources. This is an upper bound, not an exact isolated-model value. Independent validation of that inference is required.
limitations: NVIDIA per-process usage is N/A in WDDM.
D3DKMT direct process query requires PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION; access to vmwp is denied (Win32 error5) for this nonadmin executor. No escalation or permission change is attempted.

Microsoft documents a Windows GPU Process Memory counter overreporting issue; preserve that caveat and the stopped/load/unload controls. Do not claim a continuous-time or per-container exact physical peak.
mandatory_checks: two256-token decode samples with accepted MTP tokens
three native Claude tasks with pre-existing max2 feedback repairs; preserve all revisions
acceptance_not_weakened: The existing whole-host v5 result and NOT_READY full-goal verdict remain unchanged. Direct VM counters address measurement scope; they are not relabeled as exact isolated model accounting.
